prompts.prompt: Do a security-focused review of this service, covering the whole src folder. Write review.md with each finding's severity (Critical, Important or Minor), file and line, why it matters, and a concrete fix, ordered by severity. Only report real problems you can point to in the code. Do not change any code. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, list your assumptions in your final message, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: Bench task reused. The skill's checklist (input validation, specific error handling without leaking internals, atomic read-modify-write, auth wiring per route) pushes the reviewer to sweep every route and layer; a generic security pass tends to stop at the SQL injection and the stack leak and miss the unguarded stock route, the lost update, and the fail-open fallback token.

floor_checks.text: The string-built SQL in itemRepo.js is named as injection
No file under src was changed
floor_checks.check: [ "$(find src -type f | sort | xargs sha256sum | sha256sum | cut -d" " -f1)" = "ab074c2bb5475655ce96eb5e3137fd9a799c5bdfd3cc6f429e2fba9f2071312b" ]

rubric.criterion: Coverage of the seeded defects: SQL injection (itemRepo.js:22), missing X-Admin-Token check on POST /items/:id/stock (items.js:25-27), unvalidated delta/createItem input (items.js:21-26, inventoryService.js:9-11), err.stack in the 500 body (server.js:50), hardcoded fallback admin token (config.js:6), adjustStock lost update (inventoryService.js:19-25), unbounded body (server.js:36-37), non-constant-time token compare (items.js:8)
rubric.pass: At least 6 seeds found with correct file:line
rubric.partial: 4-5 seeds found, or lines mostly wrong

rubric.criterion: Impact is explained concretely per finding (e.g. anyone can change stock without the token; stack trace discloses paths; concurrent adjustments lose writes)
rubric.pass: Each finding has a specific attacker or failure scenario
rubric.partial: Impact stated generically ('security risk') for several

rubric.criterion: Severity is proportionate and ordered: injection and the missing auth check at the top tier; timing compare and body size not above them
rubric.pass: Ordering and tiers defensible, injection Critical
rubric.partial: Mostly right with one clear misrating
rubric.fail: Injection not Critical, or no ordering

rubric.criterion: Fixes are concrete and minimal: bound parameter for the LIKE, reuse isAdmin on the stock route, validate delta as a finite integer and name/qty per README rules, generic 500 body, fail closed when ADMIN_TOKEN is unset, atomic/conditional update
Reports no false positives: no path traversal, XSS, eval, or SSRF; does not change code
rubric.fail: Several false positives or code edited

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: How many real defects were found with correct locations?
Are severities right so a reader fixes the worst first?
Are the fixes ones you could apply directly?

prompts.prompt: Review only the tests in test/ (against the code in src/) for test quality before this goes to code review. Write test-review.md with findings grouped by severity (CRITICAL, IMPORTANT, SUGGESTION), each with file:line and a concrete fix. Do not change any files. Do not ask me questions; make reasonable assumptions and list them at the end of test-review.md.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's testing checklist is specific: shared fixture factories over inline data, order-independent assertions, edge cases (null, empty, boundaries), and it rates 'test passes only due to test order dependency' as CRITICAL. A generic test review comments on coverage in general and rarely spots that adjustStock mutates item '1' that a later test relies on, or that no test covers qty == reorderLevel, which hides the < vs <= bug.

floor_checks.text: No file under src or test was changed
floor_checks.check: [ "$(find src -type f | sort | xargs sha256sum | sha256sum | cut -d" " -f1)" = "ab074c2bb5475655ce96eb5e3137fd9a799c5bdfd3cc6f429e2fba9f2071312b" ] && [ "$(find test -type f | sort | xargs sha256sum | sha256sum | cut -d" " -f1)" = "92f24aa546301779781116d59134f8ade4332fe0ff1a63e6525525af527df3e3" ]

rubric.criterion: Finds the shared module state: tests mutate the seeded in-memory rows (adjustStock on '1', save of '99', nextId) so results depend on order, and rates it at the top tier
rubric.pass: Order dependence identified with the specific tests and rated CRITICAL
rubric.partial: Mentions shared state or isolation without the concrete dependency, or rates it low

rubric.criterion: Finds the missing boundary case: no test for qty equal to reorderLevel (item '2', qty 5), which would expose inventoryService.js:31 using < instead of <=
rubric.pass: Boundary gap named and linked to the real bug
rubric.partial: Generic 'add edge cases' without the reorder boundary

rubric.criterion: Recommends a shared fixture factory with per-test reset, value assertions instead of assert.ok(item.id) / includes, and missing edge-case tests (NaN, negative, null delta)
rubric.pass: All three, concrete to these files

rubric.criterion: Uses CRITICAL / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION with file:line on each finding and lists assumptions at the end
Stays on test quality as asked; does not turn into a full security review of src or propose rewriting the test framework
rubric.pass: Scoped to tests, src defects mentioned only where a test should catch them
rubric.partial: Some drift into unrelated src review

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?
focus: Did it find the order dependence and the hidden boundary bug?
Are the fixes concrete test changes?
Did it stay on the requested scope?

prompts.prompt: Review src/services and src/repository for data correctness and layer separation (handler -> service -> repository). Write layers-review.md, findings ordered CRITICAL first, then IMPORTANT, then SUGGESTION, each with file:line, why it matters and a concrete fix. Call out over-engineering if you see it, and do not propose abstractions the code does not need. Do not change any code and do not ask me questions; state any assumptions at the end of layers-review.md.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill tells the reviewer to check atomicity of read-modify-write, layer separation, and to call out over-engineering directly. Without it, reviewers often propose new abstractions (unit of work, strategy layers) or miss that adjustStock's get-then-save loses updates and lets stock go negative against the README rule.

rubric.fail: Proposes new layers or patterns as fixes
